title: A Trail for the Provision
premise: Jude Eriksen, a railroad engineer who maps closed lines to avoid the open wounds of his past, is conscripted into a rescue expedition when an upriver survey team — including his estranged brother-in-law, Tomas — goes silent. Racing a salvage fleet that wants the wreck's cargo and a monsoon that wants everything, Jude must navigate abandoned rail spurs converted to river routes with a ragtag crew who slowly become the family he refused to want. When he discovers Tomas engineered his own disappearance to hide evidence that the salvage fleet's owner caused the original wreck, Jude must choose between duty to the expedition contract and loyalty to the people beside him. In the end, he beats the fleet by one tide, exposes the truth at the cost of his career, and chooses to stay on the river with the crew he once measured in miles.
about_author: Yara Almeida is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years charting river systems before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people who find their way home by taking the long route.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Jude Eriksen's POV. Seven years after losing his wife Lena, Jude measures life in track miles, maintaining a map of closed rail lines like a private grief ledger. When a government telegram arrives demanding his expertise for an upriver rescue, he refuses — until he learns Tomas, Lena's brother, is among the missing. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by obligation.

chapters.title: The Six-Tide Clock
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the river port of Cazadero, Jude meets the expedition: gruff captain Odile Ferran, young radio operator Sef, and salvage scout Priya Raghavan. The monsoon makes landfall in twelve days; the wreck site needs six tides of favorable water to reach. A rival salvage fleet is already loading. Beat: reluctant commitment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crew travels the first leg via a decommissioned rail spur only Jude can read from his map, impressing Odile but unnerving him — the line passes through the town where Lena died in a flood. He says nothing. Beat: the past surfacing in the landscape.

chapters.title: Priya's Bargain
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals she was hired by the rival fleet's owner, Marcus Vane, to sabotage the rescue if needed; she's defected because Vane left her brother stranded on a job years ago. She offers Jude her knowledge of the river in exchange for protection. Beat: uneasy alliance, trust tested early.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The boat clears the gorge on the first good tide, but Sef intercepts a fragmentary transmission from the missing team — someone is alive, moving upstream on foot. Hope galvanizes the crew. Beat: the mission shifts from recovery to rescue.

chapters.title: The Town That Drowned
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A supply stop forces Jude through his old town, half-submerged since the flood. He confesses to Sef that Lena died there and that he mapped closed lines to avoid driving past it. Sef, orphaned young, tells him avoidance isn't the same as mourning. Beat: first crack in Jude's armor.

chapters.title: Vane's Wake
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The salvage fleet's lead ship shadows them; Vane sends a launch offering to buy out Odile. Odile refuses, but the encounter reveals Vane knows the wreck's location already — and knows what cargo it carries. Beat: the race becomes personal and sinister.

chapters.title: Third Tide, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The second tide fails; they lose a day hauling the boat over a shoal. Tempers fray, and Priya's old loyalties are questioned when equipment goes missing — later found damaged by river rot, not sabotage. Beat: found family strained and mending within a single chapter.

chapters.title: The Signal in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the fragmentary transmission, they find a survivor: surveyor Mei Ochoa, injured, who says Tomas sent the team's radio into the river deliberately. Tomas is alive and hiding — from Vane. Beat: revelation reframes the entire mission.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Mei's POV. Mei recounts how Tomas discovered the wreck wasn't an accident: Vane's company falsified channel surveys years ago, causing the sinking and covering up deaths. Tomas took the evidence and vanished inland. Beat: duty versus truth crystallizes as the central conflict.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With three tides left and Vane's fleet a half-day ahead, Odile proposes the impossible: running the flooded Karst Narrows off-schedule. Jude calculates it can be done — barely — using an abandoned rail viaduct as a cable anchor. Beat: Jude's engineering becomes the crew's lifeline; belonging takes root.

chapters.title: The Viaduct
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crossing sequence: rigging cables in rising water, Priya nearly lost overboard, saved by Jude and Sef working as one. On the far bank, Jude realizes he hasn't thought about miles or years in two days. Beat: love against duty — he's beginning to choose these people.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Vane intercepts them at a trading post and offers Jude a fortune to hand over Mei and abandon the search — revealing he knows exactly who Jude is and what he lost. Jude refuses, but Vane leaves him doubting whether finishing this will cost him the only identity he has left. Beat: temptation and self-doubt.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide, Monsoon's Edge
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The monsoon's leading edge arrives early; the fifth tide runs wild and they make the last navigable reach with hours to spare. Sef's radio catches Vane's fleet turning back — Vane won't risk his ships. He'll simply wait for the storm to bury the evidence. Beat: victory shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They find Tomas in a ruined mission station, gaunt and defiant, guarding the falsified survey documents. The reunion is bitter: Tomas blames Jude for abandoning Lena's memory, Jude blames Tomas for vanishing. Grief finally spoken aloud between them. Beat: catharsis through confrontation.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The sixth tide is their only window downriver before the monsoon closes the gorge behind them. Loading the documents, Mei, and Tomas, they run for it as the storm swallows the horizon. Beat: all-or-nothing momentum.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Passing the wreck itself, Jude dives to verify Tomas's claim firsthand and finds the hull breached from a collision with a barge flying Vane's old flag. He surfaces changed: this is no longer about reaching safety but delivering proof. Beat: conviction replaces calculation.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The monsoon hits mid-gorge. The crew fights the storm together — every skill, every bond earned across the journey spent in a single night of rope, bilge pumps, and shouted trust. They clear the narrows as the river closes behind them. Beat: climax; found family proven under pressure.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Water
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Stranded downstream with a damaged boat, the crew shelters in a rail depot Jude knows from his map. Waiting out the storm, they bury the dead from the original wreck whose names are in Tomas's documents, giving them rites the river never allowed. Beat: mourning shared is mourning halved.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Back in Cazadero, the evidence goes to the maritime board; Vane's lawyers attack, and Jude sacrifices his engineering license by testifying to what he saw in the wreck. Vane is indicted. Tomas reconciles with Jude, offering him a place on the rebuilt survey team. Beat: justice at personal cost.

chapters.title: An Open Line
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Offered a prestigious inland posting, Jude declines. He takes out his map of closed lines and begins drawing new ones — open routes, river channels, the way home. Odile offers him a permanent berth. Beat: choosing belonging over safety.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. One year later, the crew — Odile, Sef, Priya, Mei, Tomas — runs the river together, mapping channels honestly now. Jude visits Lena's grave in the drowned town and leaves not flowers but a copy of the corrected charts. He measures life in tides now, and there are always more coming. Beat: peace, arrival, home.
